text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today to $137.35, continuing a steady climb over the past two weeks (+6.05%). The gain reflects the broader energy market backdrop: U.S. crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel, and Middle East supply disruptions—Saudi Arabia shutting down its East-West pipeline after drone attacks and Houthi advances threatening the Bab el-Mandeb Strait—are keeping crude prices elevated and supporting oil company valuations, even as prices pulled back modestly on Friday after a strong weekly rally.

The wider geopolitical tension, particularly escalating Iran-linked militant activity in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf region, creates both uncertainty and a structural support for oil majors like ConocoPhillips. Supply constraints and threats to shipping routes typically sustain higher crude prices, which directly benefits companies with large exploration and production portfolios.
